# Moodle CLI 0.9.1

Sign-in no longer depends on the CLI being able to read your browser's cookie store,
and the first run walks you through whichever path works on your machine.

## First run

With no session, a terminal now shows one note and a menu instead of a hint and an
exit. Sign in in your own browser (the login page opens; press Enter and the session
is read from it), open a browser window the CLI controls, or paste the cookie. A
failed attempt comes back to the menu with the reason, and a terminal that cannot
read any cookie store skips straight to the paths that can work. Once signed in, the
CLI offers to renew the session in the background every 30 minutes; decline and
`moodle auth keepalive install` turns it on later.

## Sign-in without a readable cookie store

The store is unreadable in more places than it looks: macOS keeps it behind Full
Disk Access, which is granted to your terminal application rather than to the CLI;
Chrome's Safe Storage keychain prompt can block indefinitely; Windows app-bound
encryption and sandboxed agent terminals fail outright. Previously `moodle auth
login` read a denied store as "no session yet" and fell into a 120-second poll that
could never succeed. Three paths now cover it:

- **Browser sign-in over CDP.** `moodle auth login` launches a Chromium the CLI owns
  and reads the session over the DevTools pipe, instead of opening your system
  browser and waiting for a cookie to appear on disk.
- **Paste login.** `moodle auth login --paste` takes the cookie directly. The prompt
  does not echo and the value never reaches argv or shell history. Any paste carrying
  `MoodleSession` works, including a Network tab "Copy as cURL".
- **Browserless renewal.** Where the site enables the mobile web service, login
  captures a durable token and later commands mint a fresh cookie from it. Support is
  detected from the site's public config and cached per instance. `moodle auth
  keepalive` uses the same path, which is what lets a background job renew unattended.

A denied cookie store is detected by probing the store files directly and fails
immediately with the Full Disk Access hint, the exact paths, and the name of the
terminal application that needs the grant. Errors report the fault in front of them:
a transport failure says so, with the host and whether it timed out. A failed login
no longer deletes the cached session it was trying to replace. `moodle doctor` exits
non-zero when a check fails.

## Fixes

- **Grades table.** A due date in the Feedback column rendered as `[2min 7 days …[22m`
  because the cell was painted before the table sanitised it. Cells now carry a tone
  and the table paints them, so the date is dimmed, amber when due within two days
  and red when overdue.
- **Try lists** under screens, `doctor` and the fallback footer print one command per
  line, like the help pages, instead of a dot-separated row.
- **Wrangler download.** `moodle mcp status` on a fresh machine failed with "did not
  create the expected executable" when the home directory holds a `package.json`: Bun
  and npm walked up to it and installed Wrangler there. The tool directory is now
  pinned with its own `package.json`, and a download that still produces nothing
  reports the installer's output. The download prompt also runs before the status
  spinner starts rather than being drawn underneath it.
- **Deploy errors** keep their auth and config hints instead of collapsing to a
  generic failure.

## Upgrade

```bash
npm install -g moodle-cli@0.9.1
```

No configuration or cache format changes. Existing sessions keep working; the next
login on a supported site adds the mobile token automatically.
